data.text/markdown: THE SHOP'S WEEK
SECTION 1: THE QUESTION Who would use this, and what decision does it help them make? Two or three sentences, in words somebody outside this course would understand.

Answer Northwind Traders’ operations manager needs a report showing how the business performed over the last seven days, including today. The report will show the number of orders, total revenue excluding freight, revenue by destination country, the five products with the most units sold, and orders from this period that have not shipped yet. This will help the manager understand sales activity and identify orders that need shipping follow-up.
SECTION 2: MY PLAN BEFORE AI

1. I will keep the number of days as an input at the top of the notebook, starting with seven days.
  2. I will calculate the reporting period so that it includes today and the previous six days.
  3. I will request the orders placed during this period from the shop API.
  4. I will check the pagination information and request any remaining pages so that I collect every order in the period.
  5. For each order, I will request its details to get the products and quantities ordered.
  6. I will count the orders and add their order totals to calculate total revenue, excluding freight.
  7. I will use a dictionary to group order revenue by destination country.
  8. I will use another dictionary to add the quantities sold for each product, then rank the products and select the top five.
  9. I will identify orders that have not shipped by checking whether their shipped_date is empty.
  10. I will print the results in clearly labeled tables and generate a sentence summarizing the findings for the manager.
  11. I will save the fetched records in a JSON file inside projects/mp2/data/ and commit that file.
  12. I will check at least one result independently before accepting the report.
  13. For Going Further, I will group order revenue by date and create a chart showing daily revenue during the reporting period, including days with no orders. This will help the manager see which days generated the most revenue.
  14. I will verify that the daily revenue amounts add up to the total revenue in the main report. I will then describe what the chart shows, including the day or days with the highest revenue, in Section 9.

data.text/markdown: SECTION 7: WORKING WITH THE AGENT

The AI helped me write the code to fetch orders, calculate the report, and save the data. However, its original code for Section 4C assigned the sorted list back to unshipped_orders, which was already defined in Section 4B. When I ran Cell 4C, marimo reported that the variable was already defined. I reported the error to the AI. Following its explanation, I changed the name of the sorted list to sorted_unshipped_orders in Section 4C. This kept the original list in Section 4B and gave the sorted list a separate name. Section 5 then used the new name when displaying unshipped orders. I verified the correction by rerunning Cell 4C, which completed without the duplicate-variable error. This taught me that marimo does not allow the same variable to be defined in two different cells. The relevant code is in Cells 4B and 4C.
SECTION 8: READING IT BACK

Function 1: fetch_order_lines

This function takes two inputs: the API’s base address and the ID of one order. It requests the details of that order and returns a list of its product lines. Each line contains information such as the product name, quantity, unit price, and discount. One line I reviewed with the AI was: order_details = response.json() This line converts the API’s JSON response into a Python dictionary. The function can then access the product lines using order_details["lines"].

Function 2: fetch_orders

This function takes three inputs: the API’s base address, the start date, and the end date. It returns a list of all orders within that reporting period, including each order’s product lines. The function collects orders one page at a time. It checks for duplicate order IDs and compares the number collected with the total reported by the API. It then calls fetch_order_lines for each order to add its product details. One line I reviewed with the AI was: more_pages = data["pagination"]["has_next"] This line reads whether another page of orders is available. If the value is True, the loop requests the next page. If it is False, the loop stops after processing the current page.

My proposed change and prediction

I will change days from 7 to 14 while keeping the same reporting end date. I expect the number of orders to increase or remain unchanged because the longer period includes all the original orders plus any orders from the additional seven days. Assuming the additional orders have non-negative totals, revenue should also increase or remain unchanged. The top-five product ranking may change because products that sold strongly during the additional week could move higher in the ranking.
